short: CLOCK, BMAL1 (gene symbol ARNTL) and NPAS2 are basic helix-loop-helix PER-ARNT-SIM (bHLH-PAS) transcription factors that form the activating limb of the mammalian circadian clock. BMAL1 pairs with CLOCK or with its paralogue NPAS2 and binds the palindromic E-box CACGTG together with a small set of E-box-like variants. The complex reads seven base pairs rather than six, because a flanking A-T pair next to the core contributes to affinity. Strong circadian promoters usually carry two E-boxes in tandem six to seven base pairs apart, and it is the pair, not a single hexamer, that produces rhythmic transcription. Occupancy oscillates once a day and drives Per, Cry, Rev-erb and thousands of output genes. Because CACGTG is also the core read by MYC/MAX, USF and SREBP, sequence alone cannot assign an E-box to the clock.
long:
## The factors

CLOCK, BMAL1 (*ARNTL*, formerly MOP3) and NPAS2 (MOP4) are bHLH-PAS proteins: an N-terminal basic helix-loop-helix domain followed by two PAS domains (PAS-A, PAS-B) and a PAC extension. The bHLH contacts DNA; the PAS domains set dimerization specificity and provide cofactor and small-molecule surfaces. Neither subunit binds DNA productively alone. BMAL1 is the obligate partner, heterodimerizing with CLOCK or with NPAS2 [PMID:9576906]; BMAL2 (*ARNTL2*) is a lower-abundance paralogue. The crystal structure of the mouse CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH-PAS region shows an asymmetric, interdigitated assembly with three separate interfaces, so the subunits wrap around one another rather than pairing symmetrically (Huang et al. 2012) [PMID:22653727]. CLOCK and BMAL1 are broadly expressed; NPAS2 is enriched in forebrain and some peripheral tissues and can substitute for CLOCK, which is why *Clock*-null mice keep behavioral rhythms (DeBruyne et al. 2006) [PMID:16675400] while *Bmal1*-null mice are arrhythmic in constant darkness (Bunger et al. 2000) [PMID:11163178]. This family holds 12 motifs from JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP labeled ARNTL/BMAL1, CLOCK or NPAS2, with none flagged as probably mislabeled.

## The motif

The core is the palindromic E-box CACGTG. Each basic helix enters the major groove and reads one CAC half-site; because the hexamer is its own reverse complement, the two subunits occupy equivalent halves. A structure of the human CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH domains on a canonical E-box resolved the hydrogen-bond network and showed BMAL1 Ile80 contacting the base pair immediately 3' of the core, so the recognized unit is 7 bp, CACGTGA, with that flanking A-T pair indispensable; the same study measured single substitutions and defined two high-affinity non-canonical boxes, AACGTGA and CATGTGA (Wang et al. 2013) [PMID:23229515]. This resolves an apparent split in the databases. The methyl-HT-SELEX models CLOCK.H14CORE.0.M.C and NPAS2.H14CORE.1.M.C recover ACACATGT and ACATGTGT, the CATGTG variant, while the grade-A models BMAL1.H14CORE.0.PSM.A and CLOCK.H14CORE.1.PS.A recover CACGTG with a flanking base. The pooled consensus computed from the members is cCACGTGc; it does not contradict the literature 7-mer, because averaging a strand-ambiguous palindrome symmetrizes the flanks. The other commonly cited variant is the E'-box CACGTT. Functionally rhythmic promoters generally carry tandem E-boxes 6-7 bp apart, and the pair rather than either hexamer confers cell-autonomous rhythmicity (Nakahata et al. 2008) [PMID:18177499]; the most information-rich model here, NPAS2.H14CORE.2.S.B, is itself a tandem (CACGTGbnndaCACGTGt, about 21 bits). No member of the family can be told from another by sequence.

## Where it acts

Binding is promoter-biased. ChIP-seq in mouse liver puts most confident sites within a few hundred base pairs of transcription start sites, often in CpG-island promoters, with roughly one to three thousand sites per time point (Rey et al. 2011; Koike et al. 2012) [PMID:21364973,22936566]. Occupancy itself cycles, peaking once per day ahead of the RNA polymerase II and H3K4me3/H3K9ac rhythms it drives (Koike et al. 2012) [PMID:22936566]. Core targets are *Per1*, *Per2*, *Cry1*, *Cry2*, *Nr1d1*/*Nr1d2* and *Dbp*; the wider output program layers E-boxes with D-boxes (DBP/HLF/TEF) and ROREs (ROR/REV-ERB) so that one clock input can generate many output phases (Takahashi 2017) [PMID:27990019]. A specific hexamer is expected about 7 x 10^5 times in a 3-Gb genome under uniform base composition; CpG depletion lowers the real count, but matches still outnumber occupied sites by orders of magnitude.

## Biology and disease

CLOCK:BMAL1 was identified as the activator of *Per1* through E-boxes, with the dominant-negative *Clock* mutation lengthening period (Gekakis et al. 1998) [PMID:9616112]. *Bmal1* loss abolishes free-running rhythms (Bunger et al. 2000) [PMID:11163178] and produces early-onset aging phenotypes including cataracts, sarcopenia and reduced lifespan (Kondratov et al. 2006) [PMID:16847346]. Pancreatic-islet disruption of *Clock* or *Bmal1* causes hypoinsulinemia and diabetes (Marcheva et al. 2010) [PMID:20562852]. In humans the clock is implicated in sleep-phase disorders, metabolic syndrome and shift-work-associated disease, though the strongest Mendelian sleep-timing mutations lie in *PER2* and *CSNK1D* rather than in CLOCK or BMAL1 (Takahashi 2017) [PMID:27990019].

## Reading a hit

A CACGTG match by itself says almost nothing about which bHLH protein bound it: MYC/MAX, MXI1, USF1/2, SREBF1/2, TFE3/MITF, ARNT homodimers and HIF:ARNT all read the same or an overlapping core, and several CLOCK/BMAL models in this family have a closer neighbor in another family than within their own. Features that shift the interpretation toward the clock are a tandem pair 6-7 bp apart, an A or T immediately 3' of the core, a promoter-proximal CpG-island location, and rhythmic accessibility or expression of the nearby gene. The hit cannot separate CLOCK from NPAS2, BMAL1 from BMAL2, or either from an ARNT homodimer. Evidence codes matter: the grade-A BMAL1 and CLOCK models carry in vitro support (HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX), whereas ChIP-only models can reflect tethering to partner factors, and CLOCK/BMAL1 ChIP peaks include many regions with no recognizable E-box.
caveats: Treat a hit as "an E-box" first and a clock site only with extra evidence. The core CACGTG is shared with the MYC/MAX, USF, SREBP and MiT bHLH groups and with HIF:ARNT, and in this family several models sit closer to motifs outside the family than inside it. Nothing in the sequence distinguishes CLOCK from NPAS2 or BMAL1 from BMAL2. The non-canonical CATGTG-type models come from methyl-HT-SELEX at grade C and are lower confidence than the grade-A CACGTG models. ChIP-derived versions include indirect binding, so peak-derived motifs are not proof that the tagged subunit touched the DNA. Tandem spacing and rhythmic behavior of the locus are more informative than the match score.

timeline.finding: CLOCK:BMAL1 heterodimers were shown to activate the mouse Per1 promoter through its E-boxes, and the dominant-negative Clock mutant protein to block that activation; this tied the behavioral period mutation to E-box-driven transcription.
timeline.methods: Transfection reporter assays, gel-shift, yeast two-hybrid
timeline.open: Which E-box variants beyond CACGTG the complex could use, and how occupancy was timed in vivo, were not addressed.

timeline.finding: MOP3, later renamed BMAL1/ARNTL, was identified as the bHLH-PAS subunit that dimerizes with both circadian (CLOCK, NPAS2) and hypoxia (HIF-1alpha) partners, placing the clock E-box inside the wider ARNT-like beta-subunit class.
timeline.open: Whether the shared beta subunit left any sequence feature that separates clock sites from hypoxia sites.

timeline.finding: Mice lacking Bmal1 lose free-running behavioral rhythms in constant darkness, establishing BMAL1 as a non-redundant component of the activating limb.

Clock-null mice were found to keep circadian behavior, reversing the assumption that CLOCK is indispensable; NPAS2 substitutes for it in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, so the partner of BMAL1 is interchangeable in a way the beta subunit is not.
timeline.methods: Mouse germline knockout, behavior, SCN slice bioluminescence
timeline.open: Whether CLOCK and NPAS2 occupy the same sites genome-wide, or only overlap at core clock genes.

timeline.finding: Cell-autonomous rhythmicity was shown to require a direct repeat of two E-box-like elements spaced six to seven base pairs apart, not a single hexamer, making spacing part of the functional definition of a clock site.
timeline.methods: Reporter assays with spacing variants in cultured cells
timeline.open: Whether tandem spacing is required at endogenous loci genome-wide or mainly at the core clock promoters tested.

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the mouse CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH-PAS region showed an asymmetric, interdigitated heterodimer held by three separate interfaces rather than a symmetric pairing.
timeline.open: The construct did not include DNA, so base-specific contacts remained unresolved.

timeline.finding: Genome-wide ChIP-seq across the circadian cycle in mouse liver put most confident CLOCK:BMAL1 sites near transcription start sites, at roughly one to three thousand per time point, with occupancy itself cycling ahead of the RNA polymerase II and histone-modification rhythms it drives.
timeline.methods: ChIP-seq time course, nascent-RNA and chromatin profiling
timeline.open: Why only a small fraction of genomic CACGTG matches is ever occupied.

timeline.finding: A structure of the human CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH domains on an E-box, with accompanying affinity measurements, showed that BMAL1 Ile80 contacts the base pair immediately 3' of the core, making the recognized unit 7 bp (CACGTGA), and defined two high-affinity non-canonical boxes, AACGTGA and CATGTGA.
timeline.open: Whether the non-canonical boxes are used at endogenous rhythmic promoters.

open: Whether the non-canonical boxes AACGTGA and CATGTGA are used at endogenous clock sites is unsettled: they bind with high affinity in vitro and the methyl-HT-SELEX models in this family recover the CATGTG form, but the grade-A models and ChIP-derived sites are dominated by CACGTG.

It is not resolved what selects the one to three thousand occupied sites from the roughly 7 x 10^5 CACGTG matches in the genome; tandem spacing, pre-existing chromatin accessibility and partner factors have each been proposed, and no model predicts occupancy from sequence alone.

Whether CLOCK and NPAS2 regulate distinguishable target sets is open: they cannot be separated by sequence and NPAS2 can sustain behavioral rhythms without CLOCK, yet their tissue distributions differ.

A substantial share of CLOCK:BMAL1 ChIP peaks contains no recognizable E-box, and whether these reflect tethering through partner proteins or binding to degenerate sites below the detection threshold of current models has not been settled.
